authority_citations: ANC-035 v3 (locked, prohibition) statement: Public storage functions MUST NOT panic.
ANC-035 v3 quote: public storage functions return `Result<T, E>` with a typed error and do not panic

ANC-035 v3 scope (clarity-only rewording of v2; the v2 parenthetical crate list was illustrative, not exhaustive): plan items that write or change public storage functions in this phase, in any crate: storage traits and engine backends (such as sc-storage and sc-runtime-db-sqlite), domain stores built on generic storage (such as sc-cron's CronStore/CronStorage), and template stores
ANC-035 context: storage contract direction: atomic transactions, cron feature withdrawn (cron storage moved out of the SQLite backend into sc-cron over generic Storage<T>; ANC-034 fixtures)
ANC-035 fixtures.pass and fixtures.fail (approved, unchanged); deterministic_check: sc-lint panic rule (randlee/sc-lint#931) clean on changed storage crates

phase-d intent: PRD v2 storage and cron requirements apply; release includes sc-cron and sc-cron-commands. Owner guideline: where readings conflict, take the stricter reading. Drift review m2 (2026-11-12) ruled the quote covers public storage functions generally.
Untyped errors, Option returns, debug_assert!, and pub(crate) helpers are deliberately not probed because ANC-035 does not determine their labels.

criteria.no: No: the item is silent about panics, only generally topical about errors, or plans a panic.
criteria.unclear: Whether the item commits to not panicking cannot be determined.
criteria.yes: Yes: the item states the public storage functions do not panic.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` state that the public storage functions it touches avoid panicking (returning typed errors instead of panicking, or denying unwrap/expect/panic)? Judge presence only.

criteria.no: No such outcome is stated, including when the item is silent about panics.
criteria.unclear: It may let a public storage function panic but cannot be determined.
criteria.yes: A public storage function is stated to panic on some path.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` plan for a public sc-storage, sc-runtime-db-sqlite or template store function to panic (unwrap, expect, panic!, or a panicking assert), even on a single path? Silence about panics is not conflict; unwrap in tests and panics outside storage code are outside `anchor.statement`. Judge conflict only.

relevant.instructions: Does `item.text` touch the public storage functions described in `anchor.scope`? Judge subject overlap only.

criteria.yes: The item touches public functions of sc-storage, sc-runtime-db-sqlite or another storage engine backend, of a domain store built on generic storage such as sc-cron's CronStore/CronStorage, or of a template store.
criteria.no: The item touches none of them, including public functions that do not read or write stored data.
criteria.unclear: The item is too vague to tell.

acceptance_table.rationale: Approved ANC-035 pass fixture: public storage functions return typed errors instead of panicking.
Approved ANC-035 fail fixture: a public storage function panics via expect, which the prohibition rules out.
New public storage function that commits to a typed error rather than a panic on invalid input.
Template store (in scope) public functions explicitly avoid panics and return typed errors.
Changes public storage functions and commits that they cannot panic, matching the pass fixture's deny unwrap/expect approach.
Writes a public storage function (in scope) but says nothing about panics or error handling; silence is compliance with a prohibition.
Changes a public storage function without saying whether it can panic; neither carries nor contradicts the prohibition.
Mentions error handling of public storage functions generically without committing that they do not panic; no conflicting plan is stated.
A public storage function that is planned to panic on invalid input is exactly what the prohibition rules out.
A public storage constructor that panics via unwrap conflicts with the prohibition, whatever the justification.
README documentation of an unrelated feature; it does not write or change any public storage function.
CI toolchain work; it does not write or change any public storage function.
Boundary: returning Result does not exempt a public storage function from the prohibition; the stated panic path conflicts.
Boundary: a panic in non-storage CLI argument parsing is not a public storage function, so the anchor does not apply.
Exception: test code is not a public storage function; the item also commits that the public functions do not panic.

The quote covers public storage functions generally; a domain store's public persistence functions built over generic storage are public storage functions (context: cron storage was withdrawn from the SQLite backend into the domain crate). The item commits to typed errors and no panic.
Adds a public domain-store storage function (in scope under the general quote) but is silent about panics; silence is compliance with a prohibition.
A public domain-store storage function planned to panic on a missing row is exactly what the prohibition rules out.
Boundary: an engine backend not named in the original example list still provides public storage functions; the quote is not limited to listed crates.
Boundary: a public function in a crate that also has a store is not a storage function when it neither reads nor writes stored data; the anchor does not reach it.
